messages.content: What is the equivalent note of C in Indian musical scale? And convert the frequency 440 Hz to wavelength?

function.name: frequency_to_wavelength
function.description: Converts the frequency of a musical note to its wavelength. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

frequency.description: The frequency in hertz of the musical note. This is a float type value.

function.name: note_conversion_indian
function.description: Converts a note in Western music to Indian classical music. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

note.description: The note in Western musical scale.

message.reasoning: The user asks two things: what is the equivalent note of C in Indian musical scale, and convert 440 Hz to wavelength. We have a tool note_conversion_indian that takes a note string and returns something. We should call that tool with note="C". Then we also need to convert frequency to wavelength. There's a tool frequency_to_wavelength that takes frequency. So we need to call both tools. The user wants the equivalent note of C in Indian musical scale. The tool note_conversion_indian will give us that. Then we need to convert 440 Hz to wavelength. The tool frequency_to_wavelength will give us that. We can call both tools. The user didn't specify the speed of sound or anything else. The tool frequency_to_wavelength presumably uses default speed of sound. We'll just call it with frequency=440.
